moduleTitle: Exporting test lists and results in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Export execution run results to CSV from the Test Runs view.
Generate a shareable PDF report of test run results.

elements.description: From Runs > Test Runs, the Advanced Filters button narrows the list of execution runs to export, then Export to CSV downloads them. Exporting is also available from the Test List > Tests view. When there are more than 200 results, the CSV download still contains all of them, not just the first 200.

Testim can generate a detailed PDF report of test run results — a shareable, presentation-ready format with execution data, test coverage, and pass/fail status, suited for stakeholders who don't need the raw CSV.

bulletPoints: CSV export: Runs > Test Runs → Advanced Filters → Export to CSV (also available from Test List > Tests).
CSV export includes ALL matching results, even beyond 200.
PDF export: a shareable, detailed report with execution data, coverage, and pass/fail status.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming a CSV export truncates at 200 rows
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Believing only the first 200 results are included when exporting a large result set.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When there are more than 200 results, the CSV download still contains all of them — the 200 figure is not a truncation limit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where can you export test results to CSV from?

options.text: Runs > Test Runs (with Advanced Filters), and also from Test List > Tests.
Only from the project's Settings page.
Only from a single test's Properties panel.
CSV export is not available in Testim.

practiceQuiz.rationale: CSV export is available from Runs > Test Runs (using Advanced Filters to narrow the list) and from the Test List > Tests view.

practiceQuiz.scenario: If a filtered result set contains 500 execution runs, how many are included in the CSV download?
practiceQuiz.rationale: When there are more than 200 results, downloading the CSV will contain all of the results — there is no 200-row truncation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the PDF export of test results best suited for?

options.text: A raw, machine-parseable data dump for scripting.
A shareable, presentation-ready report with execution data, coverage, and pass/fail status.
Replacing the CLI for running tests.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about the audience — stakeholders, not scripts.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The PDF report is a detailed, shareable format with execution data, test coverage, and pass/fail status — suited to sharing with stakeholders, not for machine parsing (that's what CSV is for) or for running tests.

quickRecap.value: Runs > Test Runs (Advanced Filters) or Test List > Tests → Export to CSV; includes all results, no 200-row cap.
Shareable report — execution data, coverage, pass/fail status.
